title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.1 & 2.2 Report, Modeling Myanmar's path to a Near-Zero Emissions Power sector by 2050

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Myanmar-specific high ambition near-zero emissions pathway.

coreDrivers.policies: The scenario includes more ambitious targets for electricity demand. Fossil Fuel capacities are progressively phased out and low carbon technology additions are optimised based on NEMO optimization tools.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: OMAP aims to achieve near-zero emissions from electricity generation by 2050, by introducing constraints to limit the use of fossil fuels.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Technology capital, O&M and fuel costs affect least-cost capacity choices. Low-carbon technology should replace high carbon power generation, and the selection of technology is made based on technology costs.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP and medium population growth extracted from World Bank combined with stronger electrification and efficiency assumptions drive power generation demand growth. The growth is much more signififcant than the one forecasted by Myanmar target. Electricity demand, for example, is twice higher in 2050 in this scenario than in a scenario following Myanmar targets regarding power generation demand.

dependencies.dependency_description: The pathway assumes significantly more electrification and power demand by 2050. Current policies are not enough and cost optimisation is used to maximise investment costs while still filling demand.
The pathway plans some important increase in electricity demand. Power additions are not enough to meet demand, and 14% of electricity needs in Myanmar comes from import in 2050.
Local opposition to large hydropower already stricked in Myanmar. This scenario is more using solar potential in Myanmar due to cost efficiency and is not planning any hydro addition in Myanmar.
Adoption of efficient appliances, electric cooking, EVs and electrified industrial processes substantially raises electricity demand while reducing demand-side emissions.
OMAP requires 9 GW batteries to maintain reserve margin at a safe level above 30%. It also accounts for 3 GW imports and diversified firm generation by 2050.
As solar expansion is important in this scenario, this scenario also highly rely on battery storage, reaching 9GW of battery storage by 2050.
OMAP nearly exhausts modeled solar and geothermal potentials. It therefore doesn't build out any hydro capacity, limiting risks from breakdown due to more severe droughts.
Drought and climate variability threaten hydropower reliability. Biomass is also important in the pathway with 5GW required by 2050, on the 6GW of technical potential assessed in Myanmar.
